newsitem.title: KENYA: Summit on Zaire calls for neutral force to deploy.
newsitem.headline: Summit on Zaire calls for neutral force to deploy.

text.p: African leaders called on Tuesday for the urgent deployment of a neutral force in eastern Zaire to protect more than a million refugees dependent on a U.N. Security Council decision.
The call was in a final statement read out in front of the leaders in Nairobi by Kenyan Foreign Minister Kalonzo Musyoka.
"The summit requested the U.N. Security Council to take urgent measures to ensure the establishment of...safe corridors and temporary sanctuaries by deploying a neutral force," Musyoka said.

He said the summit, which was not attended by any Zairean representative, called on U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali and Organisation of African Unity (OAU) Secretary-General Salim Ahmed Salim to coordinate on the move.

The presidents of Kenya, Eritrea, Rwanda, Tanzania, Uganda, and Zambia and the prime minister of Ethiopia attended the talks on Africa's most serious crisis since the 1994 genocide of Tutsis in Rwanda in the same "Great Lakes" region.
OAU chief Salim, the foreign minister of the current OAU chairman Cameroon and Tanzanian elder statesman Julius Nyerere also took part in the one-day summit at State House in the Kenyan capital.
